operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_cart_items table filtered strictly by the authenticated customer's ID extracted from the authorization context. Ensure the customer account is active (status not 'deleted').

Join with ecommerce_mall_product_variants on ecommerce_mall_product_variant_id to fetch sku_code, price, stock_quantity, and status. Join with ecommerce_mall_products on ecommerce_mall_product_id to retrieve the product name and is_active visibility flag.

Apply search filters from the request body: perform a case-insensitive search on the product name if a query string is provided. Evaluate stock_quantity against zero to calculate the isOutOfStock boolean flag.

Calculate the subtotal by multiplying unit_price by quantity for each line item.

Sort results using the sort array containing literal enum values (e.g., 'created_at.desc', 'unit_price.asc', 'id.asc').

Apply cursor-based pagination using the last retrieved primary key values.

Return the paginated summary containing id, productId, productName, variantSkuCode, unitPrice, quantity, subtotal, isOutOfStock, variantStatus, createdAt, and updatedAt.
operations.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of the authenticated customer's shopping cart line items, aggregated with parent product names, variant SKUs, real-time pricing, and stock availability status.

The operation enforces strict data isolation by filtering results exclusively through the authenticated customer's identity derived from the authorization context. It joins cart records with product and variant tables to populate display-friendly fields such as product names, SKU codes, and warehouse inventory levels. A computed subtotal is generated per line item based on the quantity and the exact unit price captured at the time of addition.

Customers can filter cart contents by product name and sort results by creation date or price before checkout. The response provides an isOutOfStock flag to alert users when warehouse inventory for a selected variant hits zero.

Query the ecommerce_mall_cart_items table by matching the provided cartItemId and the authenticated customer's ID to enforce ownership isolation.
Join with ecommerce_mall_product_variants to fetch the variant SKU, stock status, and active status.
Join with ecommerce_mall_products to retrieve the base product name and main image URL.
Join with ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options to compile the list of currently selected attribute key-value pairs for the chosen variant.
Calculate a subTotal by multiplying the line item's quantity by its unit_price.
If the cart item is not found or does not belong to the requesting customer, return a 404 Not Found.

Retrieve the detailed information of a specific shopping cart line item, including its associated product and variant attributes.

This operation returns the complete record for a single cart entry. To ensure data integrity and account isolation, the request is rejected if the specified cart item does not belong to the authenticated customer.

The response includes the line item's specific quantity, the locked-in unit_price recorded at the moment of addition, and the calculated sub_total. It also enriches this data by fetching the current base product name, the variant's SKU and stock availability status, and the active attribute options (e.g., size, color) so the user can verify the exact selection they made.

operations.specification:
Extract the authenticated "customer" ID from the security context. Validate that the provided "productVariantId" references a real record in "ecommerce_mall_product_variants". Check current inventory levels to ensure positive stock availability for the requested "quantity". Reject the request if the variant is out of stock or has insufficient calculated stock.

Query "ecommerce_mall_cart_items" to check if an entry already exists matching the current customer ID and the product variant ID. If found, increment the "quantity" field by the requested amount and update the "updated_at" timestamp. If not found, insert a new record into "ecommerce_mall_cart_items" using the customer ID, variant ID, requested quantity, unit_price fetched from the variant definition, created_at set to current time, and updated_at set to current time.

Return the fully populated cart item record as the response body.
operations.description:
Add a product variant to the authenticated customer's shopping cart.

This endpoint securely enables customers to place specific product variants into their shopping cart. The system captures the exact "unit_price" of the variant at the moment of addition, ensuring price stability for checkout regardless of subsequent catalog price changes by the seller.

Stock validation is strictly enforced. Addition is immediately blocked if the variant's calculated stock equals zero or is insufficient to fulfill the requested "quantity".

To prevent duplicate entries and simplify cart management, the system performs an upsert operation. If the specific variant already exists in the cart, the endpoint updates the existing record's "quantity" rather than creating a new duplicate line item.
operations.name: create

responseBody.description: The created or updated shopping cart item, including the captured unit price and timestamps.

requestBody.description: The product variant identifier and the quantity to be added to the cart.

prerequisites.description: Product variant must be created before it can be referenced in a customer shopping cart

operations.specification:
1. Authenticate request; ensure Actor is a registered customer.
2. Query ecommerce_mall_cart_items by id matching {cartItemId}.
3. Verify the item's ecommerce_mall_customer_id matches the authenticated customer's ID. If not, return 404 Not Found.
4. Validate the provided quantity in the request body is strictly greater than zero.
5. Fetch the linked ecommerce_mall_product_variant to retrieve current stock levels. If requested quantity exceeds available stock, reject with a 400 Bad Request error.
6. Update the quantity field and refresh the updated_at timestamp.
7. Return the updated entity joined with product variant details.
operations.description:

2. Validate the provided shippingAddressId exists in ecommerce_mall_shipping_addresses and belongs to the authenticated customer.
3. Query the customer's active shopping cart items (ecommerce_mall_cart_items). If a specific list of cart item IDs is provided in the request body, filter for those; otherwise, process all active cart items with quantity > 0.
4. For each selected cart item, fetch the related product variant (ecommerce_mall_product_variants) and extract its embedded seller id. Capture a historical snapshot including purchased_variant_name, purchased_sku, purchased_price, purchased_options, and purchased_seller_name.
5. Calculate the total aggregate order price by summing (unit_price * quantity) across all processed items.
6. Attempt to process the external payment gateway delegation using the provided paymentToken. Immediately halt if payment authorization fails.
7. In a database transaction: create a new ecommerce_mall_orders record linking the customer_id, valid shipping_address_id, calculated total_price, with status set to 'paid'.
8. Iterate through each processed cart item to generate corresponding ecommerce_mall_order_items, referencing the new order, the original variant, captured seller snapshot data, and an initial status of 'paid'.
9. Permanently delete the processed ecommerce_mall_cart_items to finalize the shopping cart clearance.
10. Retrieve and return the complete ecommerce_mall_orders record.

Query ecommerce_mall_orders table by id. Verify the order exists and is in a cancellable status (e.g., paid or partially_completed). If the order status is already delivered or refunded, throw a 400 error indicating irrevocable state.

Execute the force-cancellation by updating the order's status field to 'cancelled' and setting updated_at to the current timestamp.

Iterate through all associated ecommerce_mall_order_items records. For each item, increment the corresponding ecommerce_mall_product_variants.stock_quantity by the order item's quantity. Simultaneously, create a new ecommerce_mall_inventory_records entry with reason 'admin_force_cancelled' to audit the stock restoration.

Identify and update any pending ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests or ecommerce_mall_refund_requests linked to the order's items, setting their statuses to 'cancelled' or 'voided'.

If all steps succeed, return a 200 OK response with no response body.

When executed, the target order's status is updated to 'cancelled'. The system automatically rolls back reserved inventory by incrementing the variants' stock quantities and logs these adjustments as audit records in the inventory history. Any pending customer-initiated cancellation or refund requests associated with this order are simultaneously invalidated.

This operation is restricted to admin actors and cannot be applied to orders with a 'delivered' or 'refunded' status to preserve order integrity and prevent conflicting state transitions.

operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_inventory_records table with optional filtering, sorting, and pagination.

1. Authorization & Isolation:
   - Extract the authenticated actor ID and role from the authorization middleware.
   - If actor role is seller: perform an INNER JOIN with ecommerce_mall_product_variants and ecommerce_mall_products to enforce a strict WHERE clause: ecommerce_mall_products.ecommerce_mall_seller_id = auth.actorId.
   - If actor role is admin: apply the query on the full inventory_records table without seller restrictions.

2. Filtering:
   - Apply exact string match on ecommerce_mall_product_variant_id IF variantId parameter is provided in the request body.
   - Apply numeric range filter on quantity_change using quantityChangeMin and quantityChangeMax values if provided.
   - Apply fuzzy substring matching on the reason text field using the reasonKeyword parameter.
   - Apply timestamp range filter on created_at using createdAtStart and createdAtEnd parameters.

3. Sorting:
   - Accept the sort array. Default sort behavior MUST be created_at DESC.
   - Apply tie-breakers by id ASC if no primary sort direction is overridden.

4. Aggregation & Projections:
   - Fetch ecommerce_mall_product_variants.sku_code AS skuCode.
   - Fetch ecommerce_mall_products.name AS productName.
   - Return a paginated list of summaries optimized for rapid auditing.

5. Error Handling:
   - Validate that pageSize does not exceed platform maximums.
   - Validate date ranges (startDate MUST precede endDate).
   - Throw 403 Forbidden IF a seller attempts to manually inject and access another seller's variant data.

Each returned summary includes enriched SKU and product identification for seamless financial and warehouse auditing.

Access is strictly scoped by your actor role: Seller actors are automatically and exclusively restricted to viewing adjustment records strictly linked to variants belonging to their own storefront. Admin actors possess full-spectrum visibility across the entire marketplace platform to oversee inventory data integrity and compliance.

Records are strictly append-only and immutable. No creation, modification, or deletion endpoints exist for this table, as it functions system-wide as a deterministic historical record of all physical stock level deltas.

Sellers and Administrators use this endpoint to manually adjust stock levels. The operation records the signed quantity delta and a mandatory reason detailing the adjustment cause, permanently adding to the audit-tracked inventory ledger.
operations.name: create

responseBody.description: The newly created inventory adjustment record.

requestBody.description: Request body containing the target variant ID, the integer quantity change value, and the mandatory reason text.

operations.specification:
Query the `ecommerce_mall_inventory_records` table by the `id` primary key.

To enforce scoped authorization, perform a multi-table join:
1. Join `ecommerce_mall_inventory_records` with `ecommerce_mall_product_variants` using `ecommerce_mall_product_variant_id`.
2. Join `ecommerce_mall_product_variants` with `ecommerce_mall_products` using `ecommerce_mall_product_id`.
3. Join `ecommerce_mall_products` with `ecommerce_mall_sellers` using `ecommerce_mall_seller_id`.

Authorization rules:
- For the `seller` actor: Restrict the query to only return results where the joined `ecommerce_mall_sellers.id` matches the authenticated seller's ID.
- For the `admin` actor: Do not apply the seller restriction; return matching records globally.

Return all ledger fields: `id`, `ecommerce_mall_product_variant_id`, `quantity_change`, `reason`, and `created_at`.

Return a 404 Not Found error if the record does not exist, or if the authenticated actor lacks authorization to view the matched record.

Sellers are authorized to view records for variants under their managed products, while platform administrators maintain full visibility into inventory adjustments across all merchants.

operations.specification:
Query the `ecommerce_mall_inventory_records` table to locate the record by `{recordId}`.
Execute role-based validation against the immutable ledger policy:
- If actor is `seller`, permit updating the `reason` field for improved audit logging and stock tracking. Strictly forbid `quantity_change` modification to prevent historical financial discrepancies.
- If actor is `admin`, explicitly allow correction of both `reason` and `quantity_change` fields for data integrity rectification.
- Ensure `created_at`, `ecommerce_mall_product_variant_id`, and `id` remain completely untouched by the update payload. Note that `updated_at` is absent from the schema, so timestamp management is not required during updates.
- Log the update attempt to the internal audit trail regardless of the actor role.
Return the updated record object via HTTP 200 OK response. Handle 404 if record does not exist.

Admin operators possess elevated privileges to correct the `quantity_change` delta in case of initial data entry errors. All modification attempts are captured in the internal audit trail to maintain compliance with the unalterable stock history policy.

operations.specification:
Locate the inventory record in the inventory records table using the provided recordId.
Verify that the authenticated user has either seller or admin authorization.
Ensure the record exists before attempting deletion; return a 404 error if not found.
Check actor-scoped ownership: the seller can only delete records related to their own product variants, while admins have unrestricted access.
Permanently remove the record from the database to update the inventory ledger.
Handle concurrent modification conflicts gracefully.

Error handling:
- 404 Not Found: Inventory record with the specified recordId does not exist.
- 403 Forbidden: The authenticated actor lacks the required seller or admin privileges, or attempts to access another seller's data.
- 409 Conflict: The record is currently locked due to an ongoing inventory adjustment or audit process.
operations.description:
Permanently removes a specified inventory record from the physical stock tracking ledger.

This operation provides authorized sellers and platform administrators the ability to erase individual inventory logs from the inventory records table. Inventory records automatically document physical stock quantity changes triggered by order placements, cancellations, and successful refunds, maintaining a strict ledger of stock movements.

Access is strictly controlled to seller and admin actors. Sellers can only purge records belonging to variants under their storefront, whereas admins maintain platform-wide visibility and control over ledger integrity. This action permanently deletes ledger entries and should be utilized only when resolving data anomalies or fulfilling compliance requirements.

Standard error responses (404, 403) are returned for missing records or insufficient privileges.

operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_shipping_addresses table filtered by the authenticated customer's ID obtained from authorization context.
Apply optional keyword search filtering on recipient_name, city, postal_code, country, and street_address columns.
Apply optional boolean filtering on the is_primary column to return only default or all addresses.
Sort results using the sort array from the request body, prioritizing is_primary and created_at.
Support standard pagination parameters: current page number and page size (limit).
Return a paginated list of address summaries formatted for customer address book UI.
operations.description:
List and search all shipping addresses belonging to the authenticated customer.

Provides a paginated, filterable, and sortable list of saved delivery addresses. Supports keyword search across city, postal code, street address, recipient name, and country fields. Results can be sorted by creation date or by primary status.

The response includes summary address details required for customer address book displays and checkout selection.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of the authenticated customer's shipping address summaries.

requestBody.description: Search filters (keyword, is_primary), pagination parameters, and sorting criteria for the address list.

operations.specification:
Retrieve the authenticated customer ID from the authorization context (JWT token). Insert a new record into the ecommerce_mall_shipping_addresses table using the provided request body fields (recipient_name, phone_number, country, state_province, postal_code, city, street_address, is_primary). Automatically set the system timestamp fields for id, created_at, and updated_at upon insertion.

Validate all required fields in the request body: recipient_name, phone_number, country, postal_code, city, and street_address. Reject the request with a validation error if any are missing or malformed.

Handle primary address assignment: If is_primary is true, query all existing shipping addresses for the authenticated customer, update their is_primary field to false, and then insert the new address with is_primary set to true. If is_primary is omitted or false, insert the record with is_primary defaulting to false.

Return the complete newly created address object including the generated system identifiers and timestamps.
operations.description:
Create a new shipping address for the authenticated customer's account.

Registers a physical delivery destination with complete contact and geographical routing information. The operation securely links the new address to the authenticated customer, enabling streamlined checkout processes by providing multiple valid shipping options.

If the is_primary flag is provided and set to true, the system automatically designates this address as the default shipping destination. This action demotes any previously set primary address to a standard saved state, enforcing the platform's single-default-address policy per customer.
operations.name: create

responseBody.description: The newly created shipping address record with system-generated timestamps and unique identifier.

requestBody.description: Shipping destination details including the recipient's name, contact phone number, and full geographical address components. Option to designate this address as the primary default for future checkouts.

operations.specification: Query the `ecommerce_mall_shipping_addresses` table to find a single record by its `id` column. Validate that the retrieved address belongs to the authenticated customer by comparing the `ecommerce_mall_customer_id` column against the customer ID extracted from the authorization context. Enforce cascade deletion behavior implicitly since `onDelete: Cascade` is defined on the relation. Upon successful validation, return the full address record including recipient names, contact details, geographic data, and the primary flag status. Return a 404 Not Found if the address does not exist or belongs to a different customer.
operations.description:
Retrieves the comprehensive details of a specific shipping address associated with the authenticated customer's account.

The API enforces strict ownership validation, ensuring the requested address belongs to the logged-in customer rather than relying on actor identity from the request payload. The response includes the full destination information required for logistics verification, encompassing recipient names, contact phone numbers, street, city, state/province, postal code, and country. Additionally, it provides the is_primary flag to indicate whether this address serves as the customer's default shipping destination. Returns a 404 error if the address is not found or does not belong to the authenticated user.
operations.name: at

parameters.description: Unique identifier for the shipping address being retrieved.
parameters.name: addressId

responseBody.description: Full structural details of the requested shipping address including geographic and contact information.

operations.description:
Updates a specific shipping address associated with the authenticated customer's account. Customers can modify delivery details including recipient name, contact number, geographic location, and primary status indicator.

Accepts updated address details such as recipient name, phone number, country, state or province, postal code, and detailed street address. The system validates ownership to ensure authenticated users can only modify their own saved delivery destinations.

Enforces a single default address constraint per account. If the primary flag is set to true, the system automatically demotes any previously configured default address for the customer to false to maintain data integrity and unique constraint compliance.
operations.name: update

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the shipping address to update.
parameters.name: addressId

responseBody.description: The complete updated shipping address record reflecting the new configuration and current timestamps.

requestBody.description: Updated shipping address details including recipient information, geographic location parameters, and default status indicator.

prerequisites.description: The shipping address must be created before its details can be updated.

operations.specification:
Retrieve the shipping address record from ecommerce_mall_shipping_addresses matching the provided addressId.

Verify ownership by ensuring the record's ecommerce_mall_customer_id matches the authenticated customer's ID.

Execute deletion eligibility checks before removal:
1. Query the count of all active shipping addresses for this customer.
2. If the count is 1, reject the deletion. Return a 400 error instructing the customer to designate a new primary address or update an existing one, as per the default address fallback logic mechanism.
3. If the address has is_primary set to true, reject the deletion. Prompt the customer to assign a different address as primary before proceeding.

If all checks pass, permanently delete the record from ecommerce_mall_shipping_addresses.

Return null on successful deletion. Handle standard 404 for missing addresses and 403 for unauthorized access attempts.
operations.description:
Permanently removes a saved shipping address from the customer's profile.

This operation requires the requester to be the verified owner of the address. The system enforces strict deletion eligibility rules to maintain a valid shipping destination for future orders.

If the address is the customer's only remaining entry or currently designated as primary, the deletion is blocked. In such cases, the customer must first select or create an alternative address to assign as the new default before this address can be erased.

Returns null upon successful removal.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the shipping address to delete.
parameters.name: addressId

Query the ecommerce_mall_shipments table filtered by the authenticated seller's ID (extracted from request context).
Apply optional filters on status, carrier_name, tracking_number, and date ranges for shipped_at, estimated_delivery_at, or delivered_at.
Return offset-based paginated results sorted according to the sort criteria.
Ensure all operations strictly filter by the logged-in seller's ID to guarantee data isolation.
Handle optional carrier_name search with case-insensitive matching.
operations.description:
Search and list shipments assigned to the authenticated seller. This endpoint allows sellers to browse, filter, and sort their logistics fulfillments across a paginated interface.

Supports filtering by shipment status, carrier name, tracking number, and date ranges for shipped_at and delivery metrics. Paginated by default with configurable page size and sort order. All results are strictly scoped to the authenticated seller's account.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Paginated list of shipment summaries scoped to the authenticated seller's logistics operations.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination options for filtering seller shipments.

operations.specification:
1. Validate input: ensure itemIds array is provided and contains at least one valid UUID.
2. Query ecommerce_mall_order_items for all IDs in itemIds.
3. Verify all queried items belong to the authenticated seller's account. Return 400 if any item belongs to a different seller.
4. Verify all items have status = 'paid'. Return 400 if any item has a different status (e.g., shipped, delivered, cancelled).
5. Check ecommerce_mall_shipment_items to ensure none of the provided itemIds are already linked to an existing shipment. Return 400 if a duplicate shipment item is found.
6. Retrieve the parent ecommerce_mall_orders record from the first item's ecommerce_order_id, and fetch its ecommerce_mall_shipping_address_id.
7. Begin a database transaction:
   a. Insert a new ecommerce_mall_shipments record with ecommerce_mall_order_id, ecommerce_mall_seller_id (from auth context), ecommerce_mall_shipping_address_id, carrier_name, tracking_number (if provided), status = 'shipped', and shipped_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP.
   b. Insert mapping records into ecommerce_mall_shipment_items for each provided itemIds pairing with the new shipment ID.
   c. Update all matched ecommerce_mall_order_items, setting status = 'shipped' and updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP.
8. Commit transaction and return the newly created ecommerce_mall_shipments record along with the itemCount of bundled order items.
operations.description:
Create a new shipment by bundling one or more pending order items from the authenticated seller.

This endpoint allows sellers to initiate the fulfillment process for purchased items. The seller specifies which order items to bundle together into a single shipment package. The system validates that all selected items belong to the same seller, are in a 'paid' state, and have not already been assigned to a shipment.

Upon successful creation, the shipment is recorded with the provided carrier and tracking details. All bundled order items are transitioned to 'shipped' status, reflecting that the items are now in transit.

- Throws 400 if selected order items belong to different sellers.
- Throws 400 if any selected order item is not currently in 'paid' status.
- Throws 400 if any selected order item has already been assigned to an existing shipment.
operations.name: create

responseBody.description: The newly created shipment record including carrier details, shipping status, and bundled item count.

requestBody.description: List of order item IDs to bundle, along with carrier and tracking information for the physical shipment.

prerequisites.description: The order items to be bundled into a shipment must already exist. Order items are generated as part of the customer order creation process, so a valid order must exist first.

operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_shipments for the record matching the given shipmentId.

Enforce seller-scoped data isolation: append AND ecommerce_mall_seller_id = {{seller.identity.id}} to the base query. The authenticated seller's identity must be extracted from the authorization context.

If the record is not found, return 404 Not Found.

Optionally perform LEFT JOINs with ecommerce_mall_orders on order_id and ecommerce_mall_shipping_addresses on shipping_address_id to enrich the response with order summary and destination details if the DTO structure requires it. Otherwise, return the raw shipment fields.

Return the complete shipment entity including carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at, estimated_delivery_at, delivered_at, status, and associated metadata.
operations.description:
Retrieves comprehensive details for a specific shipment managed by the authenticated seller. 

The endpoint returns carrier information, tracking number, shipping address, linked order reference, and the current fulfillment status including dispatched and delivery timestamps. Sellers can only access shipments originating from their own shop profile. If the shipment ID does not exist or belongs to another seller's inventory, the system returns a 404 Not Found response to prevent unauthorized data access.
operations.name: at

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the shipment (globally scoped)
parameters.name: shipmentId

responseBody.description: Complete shipment entity containing carrier details, tracking information, delivery timestamps, status, and associated order reference.

operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_shipments table by id (UUID) where ecommerce_mall_seller_id matches the authenticated seller's ID.

If shipment not found or seller doesn't own the shipment → return 404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden.

Apply the provided update fields (carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at, estimated_delivery_at, status) to the existing record. Use Prisma's optional update to only modify provided fields.

Validate that carrier_name, if provided, is a non-empty string (trimmed).
Validate that tracking_number, if provided, is a non-empty string (trimmed).

Do NOT allow updates if delivered_at is already set — delivery confirmation locks carrier and tracking to preserve audit trail.

Update the record with Prisma's update with new updated_at timestamp.

Return the full updated shipment record including all fields: id, parent order_id, seller_id, shipping_address_id, carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at, estimated_delivery_at, delivered_at, status, timestamps.

If any validation fails (empty string values, status conflicts, delivery locked), throw 422 Unprocessable Entity with descriptive error message.
operations.description:
Updates the specified shipment with new carrier and tracking details.

Modifies the core shipment metadata that customers use for package tracking. Sellers can update carrier name, tracking number, and delivery timing information throughout the fulfillment lifecycle. The operation enforces seller ownership validation — only the seller who created the shipment can update it.

The carrier name and tracking number are the primary fields for customer-facing tracking visibility. Updated tracking information is immediately reflected in the customer's order detail view and shipment tracking page.

Validation ensures the seller has permissions to update this shipment and that the new values don't conflict with the current fulfillment status.

Note: Once a shipment is marked as delivered, certain fields like carrier name and tracking number may no longer be modifiable to preserve the fulfillment record integrity.
operations.name: update

parameters.description: UUID of the shipment to update.
parameters.name: shipmentId

responseBody.description: The full updated shipment record including all metadata, carrier details, and current fulfillment status.

requestBody.description: Partial update fields for the shipment. Can include carrier_name, tracking_number, shipped_at, estimated_delivery_at, and status changes.

prerequisites.description: Shipment must be created and exist before seller can update its carrier and tracking details.

operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the seller and retrieve their actor ID from the session context.
2. Query the ecommerce_mall_shipments table for the record matching shipmentId.
3. Verify that the record's ecommerce_mall_seller_id matches the authenticated seller ID. Return 403 Forbidden if the seller does not own this shipment.
4. Validate the deletion eligibility by checking the status field. If status is 'delivered', return 409 Conflict as delivered shipments cannot be erased to preserve delivery audit trails.
5. If the status is 'shipped' or 'in_transit', proceed with deletion. Execute a database DELETE on the ecommerce_mall_shipments record.
6. Rely on the database CASCADE constraint on ecommerce_mall_shipment_items to automatically purge associated junction records.
7. Query ecommerce_mall_shipment_items to identify the affected order items referenced by the deleted shipment. Update their status from 'shipped' or 'in_transit' back to 'paid' to safely reverse the fulfillment state.
8. Return 204 No Content on successful removal.
9. Handle 404 Not Found if the shipmentId does not exist.
operations.description:
Erases a specific shipment container and its associated fulfillment records.

Allows the seller to permanently remove a shipment record that has not yet been confirmed as delivered. The operation is strictly guarded by ownership verification, ensuring only the seller who dispatched the package can initiate the removal. Attempting to erase a shipment marked with a 'delivered' status will be rejected to maintain compliance and delivery audit trails.

Upon successful deletion, the system automatically reverts the status of all linked order items from 'shipped' or 'in_transit' back to 'paid'. This safely cancels the physical dispatch without disrupting the parent order, leaving the transaction in an active fulfillment state for potential reshipment or alternative resolution.
operations.name: erase

parameters.description: The unique UUID identifier of the shipment container to be erased.
parameters.name: shipmentId

prerequisites.description: Shipment must exist before it can be erased. This POST operation creates the shipment record in ecommerce_mall_shipments table that the DELETE targets.

operations.specification:
1. Authenticate user and verify seller actor role. Extract seller ID from auth context.
2. Query ecommerce_mall_shipments WHERE id = {shipmentId} AND ecommerce_mall_seller_id = currentSellerId. Return 404 if not found.
3. Enforce data isolation: if the shipment belongs to another seller, return 403 Forbidden.
4. Validate shipment status constraints:
   - If status is 'delivered' or 'cancelled', reject with 422 (fulfillment already complete).
5. Parse request body IEcommerceMallShipment.IAssignRequest:
   - orderItemIds: array of string (uuid). Validate provided IDs correspond to existing ecommerce_mall_order_items.
   - Validate each referenced order item currently has status 'paid' or 'pending'. Reject with 422 for items in 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', or 'refunded'.
   - carrierName: string, maxLength 255. Optional.
   - trackingNumber: string, maxLength 255. Optional.
   - estimatedDeliveryAt: datetime. Optional.
6. Execute database transaction:
   a. DELETE existing records from ecommerce_mall_shipment_items where ecommerce_mall_shipment_id = {shipmentId}.
   b. INSERT new mapping rows into ecommerce_mall_shipment_items for each ecommerce_mall_order_item_id -> shipmentId.
   c. Update ecommerce_mall_shipments row:
      - Set carrier_name = carrierName
      - Set tracking_number = trackingNumber
      - Set estimated_delivery_at = estimatedDeliveryAt
      - If carrier_name or tracking_number is provided AND current status is not already 'shipped', set status = 'shipped' AND shipped_at = NOW().
   d. Update status of all newly assigned order items in ecommerce_mall_order_items to 'shipped'.
7. Commit transaction.
8. Construct and return IEcommerceMallShipment.ISummary with all assigned items joined and current shipment metadata.
operations.description:
Assigns or regroups order items into a specific shipment bundle and finalizes shipping metadata for order fulfillment.

Sellers use this endpoint to collect eligible items from their sold inventory and map them to a physical shipping container. The operation directly manages the junction table (ecommerce_mall_shipment_items), ensuring accurate many-to-many mapping between the shipment and its constituent order line items. Only order items in 'paid' or 'pending' status are eligible for assignment.

Providing carrierName and trackingNumber in the request body automatically transitions the shipment and all contained order items to 'shipped' status and records the dispatch timestamp (shipped_at). The system strictly enforces seller ownership, preventing merchants from modifying shipments belonging to other storefronts.
operations.name: manage

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the shipment container to manage.
parameters.name: shipmentId

responseBody.description: Updated shipment data including the assigned order items list and fulfillment status.

requestBody.description: Order item IDs to include in this shipment bundle, along with optional carrier and tracking details.

prerequisites.description: Order items referenced in the request body must exist as completed purchase line items before they can be validated for paid/pending status and assigned to a shipment.
The shipment container identified by shipmentId must exist to serve as the parent fulfillment bundle for mapping and managing order item assignments.

operations.specification: Query the `ecommerce_mall_shipment_items` table using `{shipmentItemId}`. Simultaneously verify ownership by joining with `ecommerce_mall_shipments` on `{shipmentId}` and confirming that the `ecommerce_mall_seller_id` matches the currently authenticated seller's actor ID. If the shipment is not found or the seller does not own it, return a 404 error. Upon successful authorization, eagerly load the associated `ecommerce_mall_order_items` to retrieve `purchased_variant_name`, `purchased_sku`, `quantity`, and `purchased_price`. Join with `ecommerce_mall_shipments` to include `carrier_name`, `status`, `tracking_number`, and `shipped_at`. Return a single `IEcommerceMallShipmentItem` object containing the shipment item record, mapped order item details, and shipment metadata.
operations.description:
Retrieves detailed information for a specific line item within a shipment bundle. This endpoint allows sellers to verify order item details, fulfillment status, and shipment metadata for a given line item. Access is strictly enforced to the seller who created the shipment, ensuring data isolation across merchant accounts. Returns the complete record including linked order item attributes such as product name, SKU, and quantity, as well as shipment-level information like carrier details and dispatch status.

### Authorization
Sellers can only access line items belonging to shipments they created. Requests for shipments belonging to other sellers will be rejected with a 404 response to prevent cross-merchant data leaking.

### Data Composition
The response aggregates data from the shipment line item junction, the parent order item record, and the shipment container to provide full context for inventory and fulfillment management.
operations.name: at

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the parent shipment bundle.
parameters.name: shipmentId

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the shipment line item.
parameters.name: shipmentItemId

responseBody.description: Complete shipment item record including linked order item details and shipment metadata.

prerequisites.description: The shipment must be created and contain the target order item for the shipment line item to exist.

operations.specification:
1. Retrieve the `ecommerce_mall_shipment_items` record matching `shipmentItemId`.
2. Perform a JOIN with `ecommerce_mall_shipments` to verify that the authenticated seller's ID matches the `ecommerce_mall_seller_id` field of the parent shipment record. Reject the request with a 403 Forbidden error if authorization fails.
3. If the `requestBody.status` value is provided, use it to update the corresponding `ecommerce_mall_order_items.status` field. Simultaneously, update the `ecommerce_mall_order_items.updated_at` timestamp to match the current system time.
4. Update the `ecommerce_mall_shipment_items.updated_at` timestamp to reflect the modification of the junction record.
5. Serialize the updated `ecommerce_mall_shipment_items` record, including the newly updated `ecommerce_mall_order_items.status` and related shipment metadata, into the `IEcommerceMallShipmentItem` response schema.
operations.description:
Allows sellers to manually update the fulfillment status of a specific order item linked to a shipment bundle.

When the seller modifies the status through this endpoint, the backend propagates the change directly to the atomic `ecommerce_mall_order_items.status` field, ensuring precise state synchronization across the logistics pipeline. The operation requires the authenticated seller to own the parent shipment record, guaranteeing that merchants can only alter fulfillment statuses for shipments originating from their own stores.

2. Verify that the found shipment's `ecommerce_mall_seller_id` matches the `seller_id` extracted from the authenticated seller's session claims. If mismatched, return 403 Forbidden.
3. Query `ecommerce_mall_shipment_items` to locate the record matching `{shipmentItemId}` within the validated shipment. If not found, return 404 Not Found.
4. Execute a direct `DELETE` on the matched `ecommerce_mall_shipment_items` record. Do not trigger cascading deletions on the parent tables (`ecommerce_mall_orders`, `ecommerce_mall_orders_items`).

This operation is primarily used to correct shipment groupings, split pending shipments, or withdraw an item from a dispatch queue prior to carrier pickup. Removal only affects the mapping in the shipment items table and does not cascade to the underlying order items or alter the overall order fulfillment status.

2. Query ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests table where customer_id matches the authenticated user.

4. Left join ecommerce_mall_order_items on order_item_id to fetch snapshot fields required for summary display: purchased_variant_name, purchased_sku, purchased_price, quantity, order item status, and order_id.
5. Apply sorting from the sort array in request body. Default ordering is created_at DESC if no sort criteria are provided.
6. Apply pagination using offset-based logic (offset = (page - 1) * limit, limit = requested limit) and return total count of matching records.
7. Map database status values (e.g., PENDING, APPROVED, REJECTED) to lowercase API response strings.
8. Convert created_at and updated_at timestamps to ISO 8601 format.
9. If no records match the filters, return an empty summary array with total count zero.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of cancellation requests submitted by the authenticated customer.

This endpoint allows customers to track the status of their pre-shipment withdrawal petitions for specific order items. The response includes a snapshot of the original order item details (such as variant name, SKU, unit price, and quantity) at the time of cancellation to provide full context without requiring additional API calls.

Customers can filter requests by status (e.g., pending, approved, rejected) and sort results by creation date using standard sort criteria. Each request is automatically scoped to the authenticated customer based on their session token and cannot be modified from this list view.

If the item is in any other state (e.g., 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled'), throw a 400 validation error. Check `ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests` to ensure no existing request is linked to this `order_item_id` (enforced by the `@@unique([order_item_id])` constraint). If found, return a 409 conflict. Upon validation, insert a new record into `ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests` with `customer_id` from the authorization context, `order_item_id` from the path variable, `reason` from the request body, `status` set to `'pending'`, and both `created_at` and `updated_at` timestamps set to the current time. This operation enables buyers to formally request the withdrawal of a specific line item before the seller initiates physical dispatch. Upon submission, the request is recorded in a `'pending'` state awaiting formal review and authorization by the responsible seller.

Validation enforces strict eligibility: cancellation petitions are only accepted when the targeted order item is currently in a `'paid'` state. Attempts to cancel already shipped, delivered, or previously cancelled items are rejected. Additionally, duplicate requests for the same line item are blocked to prevent redundant financial holds.

Return 403 Forbidden if the request belongs to another customer. Return 404 Not Found if the UUID does not exist or lacks authorization.

- `id`: string (uuid)
- `orderId`: string (uuid) joined from order_items -> order

- `productVariantName`: string from order items

Retrieve detailed information for a specific pre-shipment cancellation request.

This enables customers to track the progress and outcome of their withdrawal petitions without needing to fetch order details separately.

The endpoint is strictly scoped to the authenticated customer's identity. Customers can only retrieve cancellation requests created by their own account and are denied access to other users' requests, ensuring privacy across the marketplace.

Cancellation requests follow a workflow lifecycle where they transition from pending review to approved or rejected after the seller evaluates the buyer's rationale against the fulfillment pipeline.

operations.specification:
1. Query ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests by requestId via the order_item_id relationship (or direct PK access). Return 404 if not found.
2. Assert the request status is 'pending'. If the status is 'approved' or 'rejected', return 409 Conflict indicating already finalized.
3. Join orderItem via order_item_id to fetch the associated ecommerce_mall_order_items record for ownership verification.
4. Verify authorization: compare orderItem.ecommerce_seller_id with the authenticated seller's ID. Return 403 Forbidden if the authenticated seller does not own the product variant involved in this order item.
5. Validate request body: 'decision' must be exactly 'approved' or 'rejected'. Return 400 for invalid values.
6. If decision is 'approved':
   - Update ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests status to 'approved'.
   - Update ecommerce_mall_order_items status to 'cancelled'.
   - Create a new ecommerce_mall_cancellation_snapshots record, setting ecommerce_mall_cancellation_request_id, decision_maker_id (authenticated seller), decision, and the optional seller reason.
   - Insert into ecommerce_mall_inventory_records to restore stock: set delta equal to the orderItem.quantity, triggering a positive restock.
7. If decision is 'rejected':
   - Update ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests status to 'rejected'.
   - Leave orderItem.status unchanged.
   - Create a new ecommerce_mall_cancellation_snapshots record with decision, decision_maker_id, and optional reason.
8. Return the updated cancellation request entity including the newly created snapshot relation.
operations.description:
Allows a seller to review and decide on a customer's pre-shipment cancellation request for a specific order item.

The seller evaluates the pending cancellation request and issues a binding decision. Once processed, an immutable audit snapshot is appended to permanently document the seller's decision, the acting seller, and any accompanying remarks for future transparency.

Upon approval, the target order item is permanently marked as cancelled, and the corresponding inventory is automatically restored to the variant's stock level. A rejected request leaves the order item in its current fulfillment state while preserving the decision log for dispute resolution.

The server strictly enforces seller ownership by matching the authenticated user against the seller ID attached to the order item's original product variant, rejecting unauthorized cross-seller actions.

parameters.name: requestId

responseBody.description: The fully updated cancellation request record reflecting the seller's final decision, including the newly generated immutable audit snapshot.

requestBody.description: The seller's final decision on the customer's cancellation request, specifying either approval or rejection, accompanied by an optional explanatory remark.

Apply optional filters from the request body: status (equals match), keyword (ILIKE search on reason column), and dateFrom/dateTo (range filter on created_at column). Apply sorting using the provided sort array, defaulting to created_at DESC. Perform lightweight JOINs with ecommerce_mall_orders and ecommerce_mall_sellers to fetch order identifiers/summaries and seller names for the response DTO. Execute offset/limit pagination based on page and pageSize parameters. Return total count and page data. Handle edge cases where referenced orders may be archived by gracefully returning partial snapshot data without breaking the query.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of refund claims initiated by the authenticated customer.

This endpoint provides full visibility into the customer's refund request history, allowing them to track the status and outcome of financial restitution claims. Results are strictly scoped to the authenticated user's account, with the customer identity injected automatically from the session authorization context.

Customers can filter claims by their current workflow status (PENDING_REVIEW, APPROVED, REJECTED), search within the submitted reasons, or narrow the timeline using date ranges. The response includes representative summary data such as order references, requested refund amounts, and approval decisions to support dashboard and history UI screens.

operations.specification:
1. Extract orderItemId from the path parameter.
2. Query the ecommerce_mall_order_items table to retrieve the order item record matching the given orderItemId.
3. Verify that the order item exists; if not, return 404 Not Found.
4. Retrieve the parent order from ecommerce_mall_orders using the order item's ecommerce_order_id to confirm that the order belongs to the authenticated customer (compare ecommerce_mall_customer_id from the order against the authenticated user's ID from the session context).
5. If the order does not belong to the authenticated customer, return 403 Forbidden.
6. Check the order item's status field — it must equal delivered. If the status is paid, shipped, cancelled, or refunded, return 400 Bad Request with an appropriate message indicating the item has not yet been delivered.
7. Calculate the elapsed time since the delivery confirmation date. If more than 7 calendar days have passed since delivery, return 400 Bad Request with an expiration message.
8. Compute the refundAmount by multiplying the order item's purchased_price by its quantity field.
9. Retrieve the sellerId from the order item's ecommerce_seller_id field to assign the correct seller to the refund request for review.
10. Create a new record in the ecommerce_mall_refund_requests table with the following values:
    - ecommerce_mall_customer_id: populated from the authenticated customer's ID (extracted from session/token).
    - ecommerce_mall_order_id: the order's UUID from the order item.
    - ecommerce_mall_order_item_id: the orderItemId provided in the path.
    - ecommerce_mall_seller_id: the seller's UUID from the order item.
    - reason: the text reason provided in the requestBody.
    - refund_amount: the computed refundAmount.
    - status: set to PENDING_REVIEW.
    - seller_comment: null.
    - processed_at: null.
    - created_at: current timestamp.
    - updated_at: current timestamp.
11. After successful insert, return the fully populated refund request entity as the response.
12. If any database constraint error occurs during insert, handle accordingly and return an appropriate error response.
operations.description:
Initiates a refund claim for a delivered order item within the 7-day post-delivery window.

A customer may request financial restitution for a specific order item no later than seven calendar days after the item has been delivered. The system captures the customer-supplied reason for the refund and automatically computes the refund amount from the original purchase data stored on the order item record.

The operation validates the following business rules before creating the refund request:
- The authenticated customer must own the order containing the specified order item.
- The order item must have a delivered status (paid or shipped items are rejected).
- The request must be submitted within seven days from the delivery confirmation date.

Upon successful submission, a new refund request is created with status pending, linking the order item to the appropriate seller for review. The seller then has the authority to approve or reject the claim, which triggers subsequent actions including status transitions and inventory adjustments.

Enforce data isolation by verifying that the record's ecommerce_mall_customer_id matches the authenticated customer's session ID. Join with ecommerce_mall_orders and ecommerce_mall_order_items to retrieve linked order details, purchased variant name, SKU, unit price, and quantity. Include the seller_id, reason, status, requested refund_amount, optional seller_comment, and processed_at. Throw a 404 error if the refund request is not found or does not belong to the requesting customer.

Retrieves the complete details of a specific refund request associated with the authenticated customer's account.

This operation returns the full refund request record, including the reason provided by the customer, the current status (PENDING_REVIEW, APPROVED, REJECTED), the requested refund amount, and the seller's response details (such as seller_comment and processed_at timestamp) if a decision has been made.

The response is enriched with data from related entities, including the linked order item's name, SKU, price, and quantity, as well as the associated order ID. Access is strictly limited to the customer who initiated the request. Returns a 404 error if the refund request does not exist or belongs to another customer.

operations.specification:
Retrieve the refund request entity by {requestId} from the database.
Confirm ownership: the authenticated seller must match the request's seller_id.
Enforce business rule: reject the update if the current status is not 'PENDING_REVIEW'.
Validate the new status provided in the request body against allowed values: 'APPROVED' or 'REJECTED'.
If 'APPROVED', set the processed_at timestamp to the current system time.
Generate a Snapshot record capturing the pre-update state, the new state (APPROVED/REJECTED), the timestamp, and the seller_comment to preserve the decision for administrative auditing.
Update the parent order item's status to 'refunded' upon approval.
Commit the transaction and return the refreshed refund request entity.
operations.description:
Update the status of a customer's refund request by responding as the associated seller.

The seller reviews the pending refund claim and either approves or rejects it. Approving a refund request finalizes the financial decision and triggers a state transition for the associated order item. Rejecting the claim allows the seller to provide a rejection comment, which is communicated to the customer. The operation enforces that only pending requests can be updated.

Upon successful response, an immutable audit snapshot is generated to record the decision, timestamp, and rationale for dispute resolution purposes. The system validates ownership to ensure sellers can only respond to requests related to their own shop items.

operations.description:
Submits a formal application for elevated platform privileges or an administrative grade promotion.

Allows an administrator to initiate the role escalation workflow by specifying the desired administrative grade and providing a clear business justification. Upon submission, the system automatically links the request to the authenticated administrator, sets the initial workflow status to 'pending' awaiting super administrator review, and permanently records the audit trail.

The service ensures that system-managed fields such as requester identity, timestamps, and initial status are populated securely without relying on client input.

Apply filtering on status and target_grade fields based on the provided request body criteria. Enforce cursor or offset-based pagination using limit and offset parameters from the request. Sort results primarily by created_at descending, with fallback tiebreakers by id. Implement strict authorization checks at the service layer, ensuring that pending requests are exclusively visible to users with the 'super' grade to maintain platform escalation protection policies.
operations.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of administrative role request applications for platform oversight.

This endpoint allows authorized administrators to browse and filter submissions where users have petitioned for grade promotions, privilege escalations, or system role modifications. Each request entry displays the applicant's email, the target grade they are requesting, the rationale provided, and the current adjudication status (pending, approved, or rejected).

Administrators can filter requests by status or target grade, and optionally constrain results to specific creation date ranges. The system supports sorting requests by creation date or status to facilitate efficient oversight. Access to pending requests is securely restricted to super administrators to maintain platform governance and escalation protection.

Perform two joins to the `ecommerce_mall_admins` table: the first joins on `requester_id` to resolve the requester's `id`, `email`, and `grade`; the second joins on `reviewer_id` to resolve the reviewer's details. Validate that the currently authenticated admin user holds the 'super' grade to enforce platform escalation protection; if the user lacks this privilege, throw a 403 Forbidden error. If the request ID does not exist in the database, return a 404 Not Found error. Ensure cascaded relationships are honored per Prisma schema definitions.

Query admin auth context to obtain admin_id.
Validate actor_type is exactly "customer" or "seller".
Lookup the target entity in ecommerce_mall_customers or ecommerce_mall_sellers by actor_id to ensure it exists and is currently active.
Optionally verify the actor does not already have an active ban (either ended_at is null or ended_at is in the future) to avoid duplicate suspensions.
Insert a new record into ecommerce_mall_user_bans with admin_id, actor_type, reason, started_at (NOW), and ended_at (from request payload or null).
If actor_type is "customer", insert a new row into ecommerce_mall_user_ban_of_customers linking ban id to customer_id. Populate actor_session_id from request payload if provided.
If actor_type is "seller", insert a new row into ecommerce_mall_user_ban_of_sellers linking ban id to seller_id.
Revoke the target actor's active session and any other active sessions to immediately enforce the login restriction.
Return the newly created ban record from ecommerce_mall_user_bans.
operations.description:
Create a user suspension ban. This administrative operation allows platform administrators to suspend customer or seller accounts for policy violations or malicious behavior.

Upon creation, the ban record is linked to the targeted actor and associated with an existing session ID for audit purposes. The system optionally supports temporary bans by specifying an end date, after which the actor's access is automatically restored. When a ban is successfully issued, the platform automatically revokes all active sessions associated with the targeted account to immediately enforce the login restriction.

When updating the ban to remove it, the system automatically enforces the restoration lifecycle: for customers, this immediately reinstates platform login access; for sellers, it triggers the unbanned product visibility restoration, causing all storefront and product listings to immediately reappear in marketplace search and category browsing interfaces without additional configuration.

Only the fields explicitly included in the request payload will be overwritten on the server. Core identifiers such as the initiating administrator and the exact ban start timestamp remain immutable to preserve audit integrity. operations.specification:

4. After the database deletion, resolve the target actor entity from the deleted polymorphic mapping (either ecommerce_mall_customers or ecommerce_mall_sellers).
5. Trigger the platform account restoration workflow: invalidate any lingering restricted session flags, restore the user's platform login capability, and if the actor is a seller, execute the unbanned product visibility restoration routine to instantly surface their listings in marketplace search and category browsing interfaces.
6. Return HTTP 200 with no response body upon successful completion.
operations.description:

operations.specification:
Query the `ecommerce_mall_products` table to fulfill customer product discovery requests.

Apply strict filters from the request body:

- `query`: Perform a case-insensitive `LIKE` search against the `ecommerce_mall_products.name` field.
- `category_id`: Filter products strictly belonging to the specified category or its children (based on `ecommerce_mall_categories` hierarchy).
- `min_price` / `max_price`: Filter based on the `ecommerce_mall_products.base_price` range.
- `in_stock_only`: Exclude products that have zero active variants with stock available. This requires joining with `ecommerce_mall_product_variants` and filtering where `SUM(stock)` > 0.

Apply sorting rules:

- `sort` array determines the priority. Supported literal enums:
  - `"created_at.desc"`
  - `"created_at.asc"`
  - `"base_price.asc"`
  - `"base_price.desc"`

Apply pagination using `cursor` and `limit` for robust, high-performance result sets.

**Business Rules**:
- Apply strict product snapshot preservation rules for deleted products.
- Ensure 'unavailable product' rule is enforced by excluding products that have no defined and active variants.
- Ensure search is properly restricted based on `ecommerce_mall_products.status`.
operations.description:
Searches and lists marketplace products with advanced filtering and sorting capabilities.

Customers can search products by name, filter by category, price range, and stock availability, and sort results by creation date or price. Products without available variants are automatically hidden from search results. The operation returns paginated product summaries for efficient browsing.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: A paginated cursor-based collection of product summaries that match the search criteria, sorted according to the specified order.

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for product discovery, including query string, category filter, pricing constraints, stock availability, sort order, and pagination parameters.

operations.specification: Query the ecommerce_mall_categories table ensuring deleted_at is null. Resolve the self-referencing childCategories relation via ecommerce_mall_categories_id to construct a strictly two-level hierarchy. Apply case-insensitive filtering on name and optional parentCategoryId scoping if provided in the request body. Order root categories by name ascending as primary key, using id as a deterministic tiebreaker. Apply cursor-based pagination exclusively on root-level categories. Fetch and nest immediate child subcategories for each displayed parent without exceeding the one-level nesting limit.
operations.description:
Retrieves the complete hierarchical category tree to facilitate customer product discovery and storefront navigation.

Customers can browse the marketplace taxonomy by fetching active category groupings, which include display names, descriptions, and nested subcategories. The response automatically filters out categories marked for deletion, ensuring customers only interact with valid classification structures. The hierarchical data strictly adheres to the platform's maximum two-level nesting limit for optimized browsing performance.

Endpoints support cursor-based pagination, case-insensitive name filtering, and optional parent category scoping to efficiently serve large catalogs without overwhelming client memory.
operations.name: index

responseBody.description: Paginated list of active root categories with fully resolved first-tier subcategory trees, optimized for storefront navigation menus.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters including optional category name filtering, sorting priorities, and cursor offset for fetching the product taxonomy.

operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_product_variants table for all variants where ecommerce_mall_product_id matches the productId path parameter.
Join with ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options to aggregate option key-value pairs per variant (e.g., size, color).
Filter out variants with status 'unavailable' unless explicitly requested in search filters.
Return fields: id (variant UUID), skuCode, stockQuantity, status, price, and variantOptions (array of {key, value}).
Apply cursor-based pagination with page size from the request body.
Return 404 if the product identified by productId does not exist.
No authorization check is required beyond standard customer actor access since this is a public browsing operation.

Retrieves the current stock status and availability information for all variants of a specific product.

Returns a paginated list of all active product variants belonging to the specified product, including their SKU codes, current stock quantities, availability statuses, prices, and associated option attributes (such as size or color). This endpoint allows customers to check variant availability before attempting to purchase items.

The response includes pagination metadata and supports search filtering by status and option attributes. If the specified product does not exist, a 404 Not Found error is returned. If the product has no variants, an empty results list is returned.

operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated seller's identity from the authorization context (actor ID).

Execute database queries to aggregate shop metrics:
- 'totalProductCount': SELECT COUNT(id) FROM ecommerce_mall_products WHERE ecommerce_seller_id = '{sellerId}'
- 'orderItemsAwaitingFulfillment': SELECT COUNT(id) FROM ecommerce_mall_order_items WHERE ecommerce_seller_id = '{sellerId}' AND status = 'PAID'
- 'pendingCancellationRequests': SELECT COUNT(cr.id) FROM ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests cr JOIN ecommerce_mall_order_items oi ON cr.order_item_id = oi.id WHERE oi.ecommerce_seller_id = '{sellerId}' AND cr.status = 'PENDING'
- 'pendingRefundRequests': SELECT COUNT(id) FROM ecommerce_mall_refund_requests WHERE ecommerce_mall_seller_id = '{sellerId}' AND status = 'PENDING_REVIEW'

Return the aggregated summary. Gracefully handle cases where the seller has no records in any category by initializing all counts to 0.
operations.description:
Retrieves the authenticated seller's dashboard summary, providing a centralized overview of their shop's operational health.

The response aggregates key metrics including the total count of active product listings currently published in the marketplace. It details the number of order items awaiting physical fulfillment along with the counts for pending cancellation and refund requests that require the seller's immediate review and administrative action.
operations.name: at

responseBody.description: Aggregated shop summary metrics for the authenticated seller including product count, fulfillment queue size, and pending administrative requests.

Query ecommerce_mall_seller_approvals table filtering by the authenticated seller's id extracted from the seller session context.
Select the single matching approval record.
Map database columns to response DTO fields: status, rejectionReason (nullable), isSuspended, createdAt, updatedAt.
If no record matches the seller, throw a 404 Not Found error.
Return 200 OK with the formatted approval object.

Retrieves the current approval status and account state for the authenticated seller.

The response includes the operational stage of the vetting process (pending, approved, or rejected), any administrative rejection reasoning provided, and the current account suspension status. This endpoint is essential during login flows and the seller dashboard to determine whether full platform features and catalog management are unlocked.

Authenticate the seller actor using their active session token.

Query the `ecommerce_mall_seller_profiles` table to check if a storefront record already exists for this seller by filtering on `ecommerce_mall_sellers_id`. If an existing record is found, return HTTP 409 Conflict with a clear error message indicating that the storefront has already been created.

If no existing record is found, insert a new row into `ecommerce_mall_seller_profiles`. Set `ecommerce_mall_sellers_id` to the authenticated seller's `id` extracted from the session context. Populate `shop_name`, `shop_description`, and `logo_url` from the request body fields. The database will automatically generate the `id` as a UUID and set `created_at` and `updated_at` to the current timestamp.

Commit the database transaction and return the newly created profile record as the response. Validation errors for missing or malformed request fields should return HTTP 400 with descriptive field-level error messages. Database constraint violations should be caught and translated to appropriate HTTP errors.

Create a new storefront profile to establish a seller's public-facing identity on the marketplace platform.

When an approved seller decides to launch their shop, they provide the required storefront details including a public shop name, a business description, and a logo image URL. The system validates these inputs and links the profile to the seller's authenticated account. A new profile is generated if one does not already exist for this seller; attempting to create a duplicate storefront results in a conflict response to maintain single-storefront integrity.

responseBody.description: The complete newly created storefront profile record containing all identifiers, business details, and system-assigned timestamps.

operations.specification:
Retrieve the authenticated seller's record from `ecommerce_mall_sellers` using the access token context.

Validate deletion eligibility by querying `ecommerce_mall_order_items` linked to seller-owned variants for any items with a `paid` or `shipped` status.
Check `ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests` and `ecommerce_mall_refund_requests` for any records with a `pending` or `pending_review` status associated with the seller.

If any blocking conditions are found, return HTTP 409 Conflict with a descriptive error detailing the outstanding obligations.

If eligible, execute a soft-delete sequence:
1. Permanently remove the storefront identity from `ecommerce_mall_seller_profiles` (shop name, logo, description).
2. Dismantle active listings in `ecommerce_mall_products` by marking them as inactive/soft-deleted.
3. Update the `ecommerce_mall_sellers` record to mark the account as deleted.
4. Invalidate all active JWT sessions for the seller.

Preserve all historical order records, product snapshots, and shop names in read-only tables for business transparency and audit trails.

Return HTTP 200 OK with an empty response body.
operations.description:
Initiates the account deletion process for the authenticated seller's business account.

The system enforces a strict eligibility verification to guarantee all active financial and fulfillment obligations are resolved. The deletion will be blocked if the seller possesses any outstanding orders with `paid` or `shipped` status, or if there are unresponded cancellation or refund requests pending review.

If eligibility criteria are satisfied, the seller's account, storefront profile, and branding are immediately removed from public marketplace listings using a soft-delete mechanism. This preserves all historical order records, product snapshots, and shop identifiers within the database for business transparency and audit trails.

Upon successful initiation, all active authentication sessions are immediately invalidated to terminate platform access.
operations.name: erase

operations.specification:
Realize Agent must enforce strict `admin` actor authorization before executing the query.

Query the `ecommerce_mall_seller_approvals` table with incoming filter criteria from the request body. Apply exact match filtering on the `status` field if `status` is provided in the request (pending, approved, rejected). Apply boolean filtering on `isSuspended` if that parameter is provided. Execute left-join with the `ecommerce_mall_sellers` table to resolve linked seller metadata (`email`, `shopName`) when `ecommerce_mall_sellers_id` is populated. For pending registrations without a mapped seller account, seller fields must resolve to `null`.

Apply sorting via the `sort` parameter array to order by `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `id` as appropriate. Return a paginated dataset mapped as `IEcommerceMallSellerApproval.ISummary` DTOs.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filterable list of seller registration requests for platform oversight.

Administrators can query this endpoint to monitor the seller onboarding process, review pending applications, and track historical approval or rejection records. The interface returns a structured dataset optimized for administrative dashboards, including application status flags, suspension states, linked seller information, and relevant timestamps.

Administrators can filter requests by vetting status (pending, approved, rejected), toggle suspension state filtering, and apply custom sorting and pagination controls.

Return a single JSON object containing the total seller count, the count of active approved sellers, and the count of suspended or unverified sellers. No pagination is needed as this returns a single snapshot object.
operations.description:
Provides an aggregated snapshot of seller platform health and high-level administrative overview metrics.

This endpoint is exclusively accessible to platform administrators, allowing them to quickly assess the current state of the seller ecosystem without loading detailed individual records. It dynamically aggregates seller account data to provide real-time counts for various operational buckets, including total sellers, approved merchants, suspended accounts, and unverified registrations.

The metrics are computed directly from the seller accounts table via internal aggregation queries. This delivers a synchronous, lightweight response that reflects the latest registration and status changes, ideal for dashboard visualizations.
operations.name: at

responseBody.description: Aggregated platform metrics detailing seller account status distribution, registration volume, and overall seller participation metrics tailored for administrative dashboarding.

operations.specification:
Identifies the authenticated customer via the authorization session context.
Deletes all records from the ecommerce_mall_cart_items table where the ecommerce_mall_customer_id matches the authenticated customer's ID.
Validates that no active checkout transaction is currently attached to the cart items before deletion to prevent data consistency issues.
Returns a 200 OK status upon successful cleanup.
operations.description:
Removes all items from your shopping cart, resetting it for a new shopping session or canceling pending modifications.

This endpoint permanently purges all line item records associated with your account, including variant selections, quantities, and historical unit prices. The operation is designed to be atomic, ensuring the database state remains consistent even if multiple requests are sent concurrently. If an active checkout process references these items, the system will invalidate the transaction context.
operations.name: erase

operations.specification:
Retrieve the order from ecommerce_mall_orders using orderId. Verify that the order's customer_id matches the authenticated customer's ID from the authorization context.

Retrieve the shipment from ecommerce_mall_shipments matching shipmentId and the order's ID.

Validate that the shipment's status is not already 'delivered'. If it is, return a 409 Conflict error.

Update the ecommerce_mall_shipments record to set status to 'delivered' and set delivered_at to the current timestamp.

Join ecommerce_mall_shipment_items with ecommerce_mall_order_items on shipment_id. Update all matched order items' status to 'delivered'.

Fetch and return the complete shipment entity including joined order items.
operations.description:
Confirms delivery of a specific shipment within an order. Updates the shipment status to delivered and transitions all associated order items to delivered status, finalizing the logistics lifecycle for these items.

This endpoint is exclusively accessible to the customer who originally placed the order. The system verifies order ownership against the authenticated user's session before processing. Attempts to confirm an already-delivered shipment will be rejected with a conflict error.

The operation atomically updates the shipment record with the confirmation timestamp and cascades the delivered status to every order item linked through the shipment junction table. This transition triggers downstream automated processes, including review eligibility and inventory finalization.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the order scoped to the customer's order history.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the shipment whose delivery is being confirmed.

responseBody.description: The updated shipment record with delivery status confirmed and transit finalized.
